correctness.rationale: An independent field implementation verified the primitive power cycle and rank 10 for the two-zero parity checks on 242 coordinates. Matching oriented pairs of signed two-position syndromes with inverse syndromes on disjoint supports gave 145200, 203280, 261360 ordered matches. Every weight-four word has exactly three unordered two-plus-two partitions and two orders of the parts, hence the exact counts are 24200, 33880, 43560. As a second calculation, enumerating each 3^10-word dual and independently evaluating the ternary MacWilliams coefficients for weights 0 through 4 gave (1,0,0,0,24200), (1,0,0,0,33880), (1,0,0,0,43560), respectively. This also confirms minimum distance four without inferring it from the pair-bucket calculation alone. If two codewords of weight four on a common support were independent, a linear combination would cancel a nonzero position and give a nonzero word of weight at most three. Thus each support has exactly two scalar representatives, giving the three asserted support counts. Monomial maps preserve weight multiplicities, so the distinct counts establish pairwise inequivalence among the three codes.
residual_risks: These are exact finite counts for these three codes alone. No full classification of optimal length-242 ternary cyclic codes or conclusion for other extension degrees follows.

evidence: The Frobenius cosets of 2, 16, 20 are {2,6,18,54,162}, {16,48,144,190,86}, {20,60,180,56,168}; replacing an exponent by a coset-mate leaves the check unchanged. There is also a monomial alias: multiply coordinate j by (−1)^j, shifting the two exponents to 122 and e+121, then swap the checks and use the coordinate permutation j=k(e+121)^(−1) mod 242. This gives exponents 1 and 122(e+121)^(−1) mod 242, namely 182, 174, 236 in order.

The trace code defined in §III of Ding–Gao–Zhou is the dual of the two checks by nondegeneracy of the trace pairing. Thus its Example 4.5 at v=182 supplies the exact dual spectrum for a monomial alias of the target e=2.
Ding–Helleseth's e=4 example has the same dual weight enumerator, but weight enumerator agreement does not show equivalence to that example.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Compared both exponents and duality conventions. Applying MacWilliams to the known v=182 distribution yields 24200 exactly for e=2; this is real prior coverage of one component. No enumerator for e=16 or e=20 under the inspected aliases was identified. The known three-weight dual examples cannot be identical to either 11-nonzero-weight dual in the independent computation.

The weight-four counts for e=16 and e=20 and the resulting three-way distinction are not supplied or implied by the inspected construction theorems, tables, and spectrum examples. value.rationale: The choice is a comparison of canonical distance-four construction families at a common small nondegenerate admissible extension degree, not a search for an arbitrary anomalous length. At equal length, dimension and minimum distance, the exact leading weight coefficient tracks the multiplicity of minimum words and supports, and here separates three codes up to monomial equivalence by a concrete invariant. The previously covered e=2 value serves only as a baseline. The two residual exact coefficients and their inequivalence consequences are useful for identifying and comparing optimal constructions even without a general weight-distribution theorem.
residual_risks: No claims of improved minimum distance, all-weight classification, design structure, or inequivalence of additional families.
